title: Sanjay Chandra v. Central Bureau of Investigation
ratio: The primary purpose of bail in criminal trial is to ensure the presence of the accused at trial. Deprivation of liberty must be considered a punishment unless required to prevent flight or tampering with evidence. Seriousness of charge alone without evidence of flight risk cannot justify indefinite incarceration.

paragraphs.text: In bail applications, generally, it has been laid down from the earliest times that the object of bail is to secure the appearance of the accused person at his trial by reasonable amount of bail. The object of bail is neither punitive nor preventative.

Deprivation of liberty must be considered a punishment, unless it can be required for social defense or to prevent the accused from fleeing or tampering with evidence. When the charge sheet has already been filed, the detention of the accused as an undertrial prisoner is unnecessary unless apprehension of flight risk is established.
